content: Other men live to eat, while I eat only to live.
author: Socrates
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. We are conditioned to believe that more is always better—more possessions, more accomplishments, more stimulation. Yet our accumulation usually brings more anxiety, maintenance, and mental clutter.

Across his life and work, Socrates saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Wealth is not having endless things; it is wanting very little. When you realize that your deepest needs for peace, connection, and purpose cannot be bought, you become truly unshakeable.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
